chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Asimi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his uncle Ya'qub ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'What is your view of the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'It is not permissible for you [to take more] women after this'? He said: 'Rather, the women who were not permissible for him were those whom Allah prohibited for him in this Verse:
Forbidden to you are your mothers and your daughters

in this Verse, all of it. And had the matter been as they are saying, it would have been permissible for you what was not permissible for him, because one of you changes [wives] whenever he wishes, but the matter is not as they are saying.

The narrations of the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) are different from the narrations of the people. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, permitted for His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) to marry from the women whatever he wished, except what was prohibited for him in Surah Al-Nisa, in this Verse.

key_terms.حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ أُمَّهاتُكُمْ وَ بَ: Forbidden to you are your mothers and your daughters
key_terms.لا يَحِلُّ لَكَ النِّسَاءُ: It is not permissible for you [to take] women

ai.seo_question: What is the specific meaning of 'It is not permissible for you to take women after this' regarding Prophet Muhammad's marriages?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the Prophet’s restriction to four wives was a specific divine limitation rather than a general permission to marry any woman, as the verse in Surah Al-Nisa explicitly prohibits his mothers, daughters, and sisters. This distinction refutes the view that the Prophet could marry any woman he desired, emphasizing that his unique legal status included both exclusive permissions and exclusive prohibitions. The hadith underscores the principle that the Prophet’s marital laws were distinct from those of the general community, reflecting his special spiritual and juridical standing.
